title: The Endless Portrait
premise: Sebastian Eastwick returns to the decaying family estate to bury his twin brother Julian, only to learn at the graveside that the body in the casket is not Julian. As Sebastian documents every anomaly in a ritual notebook, an excavation crew for the new foundation unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, and behind it, portraits of every Eastwick child painted across two centuries, each one still wet. The house has been counting its children, keeping them, and Julian never left. To save the surviving family, Sebastian must trade his own invisibility for their escape, letting himself be seen by whatever paints the portraits before the harvest moon rises.
about_author: Coral Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed estates in New England before turning to horror. She writes about families that keep records of things better left undocumented.

chapters.title: The Wrong Brother
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the open casket, Sebastian recognizes instantly that the face is not Julian's, though everyone else insists it is. He begins his documentation notebook as a coping ritual, sketching the stranger's hands, which bear no Eastwick scar. Emotional beat: grief curdling into disorientation, the first crack in belonging.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Haunted House
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cataloguing the estate for the funeral, he finds Julian's room untouched but dusted daily, and a guest ledger listing arrivals with no departures. His cousin Maren admits she stopped counting family members years ago because the number kept changing. Emotional beat: dread disguised as tidiness; loyalty to family vs. suspicion of it.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Dario, the excavation foreman. His crew breaks ground for the funeral tent foundation and strikes a stone door beneath the east lawn, sealed from the inside with iron bolts turned outward-in. Through a hairline gap, warm air breathes out smelling of oil paint. Emotional beat: working-class pragmatism meeting something that refuses explanation.

chapters.title: The Portraits Below
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Against Uncle Aldous's furious objections, Sebastian and Dario pry the door enough to see a gallery corridor lined with portraits of Eastwick children across generations, all freshly varnished, eyes following light. One canvas is half-finished: a man with Sebastian's face. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation; documentation becomes evidence of being hunted.

chapters.title: Aldous Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Confronting Aldous, Sebastian learns fragments: the family pays a tithe every generation, one child 'kept' so the rest may leave freely, and Julian was chosen decades ago. Aldous burns part of the ledger to hide the count. Emotional beat: rage at inherited complicity; justice outside any law the family wrote.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals she saw Julian alive three weeks ago, standing at the sealed door, asking her not to tell, because he'd finally been 'finished.' She stayed silent to protect her own daughter from being counted next. Emotional beat: loyalty as betrayal; the cost of silence measured in siblings.

chapters.title: The Count Is Short
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Dario cross-checks the ledger against the portraits and finds the house is owed one more Eastwick before the harvest moon, and the half-finished portrait has gained shoulders overnight. Crew members begin refusing to work; one vanishes, leaving his boots at the door. Emotional beat: mounting panic, the countdown made visible.

chapters.title: Getting the Family Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian organizes a mass departure before moonrise, forging travel documents and loading cars, but the roads loop back to the estate no matter which direction they drive. The house will not release its count unpaid. Emotional beat: desperate solidarity fracturing under fear; some relatives turn on each other.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. At the door, the painter waits, brush loaded, and offers the old bargain: one kept, the rest freed. Sebastian sits for the portrait willingly, documenting his own surrender in the notebook's final pages, while Maren drives the last car through a gate that finally opens. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship; choosing to be seen so others can vanish.

chapters.title: Still Wet
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Maren receives Sebastian's notebook by post, final entry unfinished mid-sentence. In a gallery catalogue from an anonymous estate sale, there is a completed portrait titled 'The Endless Portrait,' its paint described as never fully drying, its subject smiling. Emotional beat: mourning braided with terrible peace; truth preserved even where justice failed.
